name: thehackernews
note: Cybersecurity news. Good for exploit write-ups and vuln post-mortems; skip breach-of-the-week stories with no technical detail.

name: 404media
note: Independent tech/surveillance journalism (Koebler, Maiberg, Cole, Cox). Good for investigations with a real mechanism — how a surveillance tool actually works, what a leaked dataset actually shows. Skip the 'Behind the Blog' meta posts and general culture-war pieces with no technical core.

name: shnatsel
note: Sergey Davidoff (shnatsel), Rust performance and correctness. SIMD in Rust, numeric edge cases (he found the musl/Rust fmaf subnormal bug), and LLM-assisted auditing of Rust crates. Good for a mechanism-first bug hunt rather than an announcement.

name: sebsite
note: C as it actually runs vs. as the standard and libc document it — glibc/musl divergences, errno and math_errhandling, stale man pages. Good for the spec/source/binary gap with a reproduction.

name: shirriff
note: Ken Shirriff (righto.com). Die photos and microcode: what a chip actually computes, often past what the datasheet diagram shows. Good for a mechanism you can follow gate by gate, including the 8087's floating-point hardware. Skip a teardown that never gets to the algorithm.

name: haxx
note: Daniel Stenberg, curl and HTTP. The recent items are often project news. Skip license, team, AI-policy, and release-announcement posts. Read one where a protocol edge or a bug has a trace of what curl or the server actually did.

name: filippo
note: Filippo Valsorda. Cryptography and TLS: a construction or a verification you can read line by line (how the NIST curve seeds were generated, a small ML-DSA verifier). Skip a policy roundup with no mechanism.

name: potaroo
note: Geoff Huston. DNS and routing measurements, especially the root KSK roll and what validating resolvers actually did. Skip the economics, policy, and cable columns that have no protocol mechanism.

name: tzannounce
note: IANA tz-announce. Paul Eggert's release notes for the time zone database, a few a year. The story is the data change: a region drops DST, and the note explains the temporary model because CLDR or POSIX cannot represent it yet. Skip a release that is only a typo or a commentary fix.

name: databasearchitects
note: Database Architects (TUM: Viktor Leis, Thomas Neumann, and co). Query execution, locking, and how an engine compares and plans values. Skip a post whose whole point is a language-feature microbenchmark with no query or storage mechanism.

name: ttaylorr
note: Taylor Blau's GitHub posts, mostly Highlights from Git x.y. Read for a behavior change in the release (on-disk format, fetch, pack), then the commit or the doc. Skip GitHub product posts and vulnerability announcements that are only a CVE list.

name: bernsteinbear
note: Max Bernstein. Language implementation: object representation, JITs, compilers emitting code at runtime. The January 2024 item is an RSS-only apology with no URL; skip it. Skip a post that is only a course announcement.

name: corsix
note: Peter Cawley (corsix). Instruction encoding, numeric approximations, and what a compiler or a CPU actually accepted. Good for a spec-versus-bits post outside the C library. Skip a note with no encoding, approximation, or compiler mechanism.

name: bitsgalore
note: Johan van der Knijff. Legacy file formats, a few posts a year: what the bytes mean, and which readers still disagree with the spec (Quattro, Multiplan, TIFF). Skip a post that only gets an old program running in an emulator and never opens the format.
